summary: The two most important predictors of income class are 'capital-gain' and 'marital-status', which are effectively tied for #1 (they trade the top rank depending on the model/split) and are both clearly ahead of the rest of the field; 'education-num', 'relationship', 'occupation', and 'age' form a second tier of moderately important features, while 'race' and 'native-country' contribute almost nothing.
primary_metric_name: top feature permutation importance (ROC-AUC drop, held-out test set)
methodological_choices: Dropped rows with missing values (coded '?', ~7% of rows). Dropped 'fnlwgt' (a census sampling weight, not a demographic signal) and 'education' (redundant string duplicate of 'education-num'). One-hot encoded categoricals, passthrough numerics for the Random Forest (300 trees, min_samples_leaf=2); standardized numerics + one-hot for a Logistic Regression cross-check. No class-imbalance correction applied (label split ~76/24, handled adequately by ROC-AUC). 75/25 stratified train/test split. Primary importance method: permutation importance (ROC-AUC drop) on the held-out test set, chosen over RF impurity importance because impurity importance is biased toward high-cardinality categorical features. One-hot importances were summed back to the original feature for fair comparison against numeric features. RF impurity importance and mutual information were computed as additional cross-checks.
verification_method: 5x repeated 5-fold stratified CV (5 different random seeds, 25 total train/val splits), refitting the Random Forest and recomputing permutation importance on each held-out fold, tracking which feature ranked #1 each time and its mean importance across all runs. Also computed a 200-resample bootstrap 95% CI for the top feature's permutation importance on the original held-out test set.
verification_result: Partially held, with an important refinement: on the original 75/25 holdout split, 'capital-gain' narrowly edged out 'marital-status' (0.0440 vs 0.0429). Under repeated CV, this ordering was NOT stable: 'marital-status' actually ranked #1 more often (15/25 folds) than 'capital-gain' (10/25 folds), and their mean importances across all 25 runs were nearly identical (marital-status 0.0436 vs capital-gain 0.0428, a gap of ~0.001 -- within run-to-run noise). RF impurity importance and the Logistic Regression permutation importance both ranked 'marital-status' clearly first, while mutual information ranked 'relationship' and 'marital-status' just ahead of 'capital-gain'. The bootstrap 95% CI for capital-gain's holdout importance, [0.0386, 0.0502], excludes 0, confirming it is a genuinely important feature, but does not by itself establish it beats marital-status. Revised conclusion: rather than a single dominant feature, 'capital-gain' and 'marital-status' should be reported as a statistically indistinguishable top pair, both far ahead of the remaining features (education-num, relationship, occupation, age), with 'race' and 'native-country' consistently least important across every method tried.
